subject.title: Version committed server-side after client 120s timeout is stuck hidden (versions:0, updatedAt frozen ~29h) — @borglife/plugin@0.2.1-beta.1

question: Should nonterminal package publish attempts gain an owner-visible status and safe retry/cancel contract, or remain operator-only with automatic recovery and clearer CLI results?
rationale: The immediate package recovery requires privileged operational inspection, while exposing pending artifacts and retry/cancel controls changes the registry’s publishing and security-scan trust boundary.

options.title: Recover now, then add bounded self-service
options.body: Recover or clear this attempt operationally, then design owner-visible status plus narrowly authorized retry/cancel behavior for nonterminal attempts.

options.title: Keep recovery operator-only
options.body: Add watchdog/retry finalization and improve timeout messaging, but retain all pending-attempt disposition behind operator tooling.

recommendation.title: Recover now, then add bounded self-service
recommendation.body: Recover or clear this attempt operationally, then design owner-visible status plus narrowly authorized retry/cancel behavior for nonterminal attempts.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged CLI timeout work is the strongest available history signal for the client-side half of the affected publish path.
